title: LATE VICTORIAN PAINTING ON BOA...
description: LATE VICTORIAN PAINTING ON BOARD, SEPIA TONES SIGNED KEITH BALLATE, H-59 W-42 CM
findings: Four photos. Framed under glass in a plain light timber frame with a gilt slip, which looks like a later frame rather than Victorian. The picture is a sepia (monochrome) painting of a young girl in a white bonnet and dress seated on a bench feeding a bull-terrier type dog that stands on a straw basket. Close-ups show real brushwork and some raised paint (straw, white highlights on the paws), so it does appear hand painted on board and not a print. The drawing is naive in places (the dog's paws look like toes), which points to a copyist or amateur rather than a trained Victorian painter. The composition looks like a copy after a popular Victorian child-and-dog subject. Writing read: painted capitals reading 'BALLAT...' on the background at upper right, cut off by the frame rebate so the last letter is hidden; this is only partly consistent with the catalogue 'Keith Ballate'. Below it is another painted line that reads roughly 'PEN... / ...YOUN...' which may be part of the picture (a wall poster) rather than a signature. Tiny writing on the dog's collar tag and on a paper scrap in the straw is not legible at this resolution. A short dark stroke near the lower right edge may be a monogram but is unreadable. No artist of the name Keith Ballate turned up in a web search, so the signature and the 'late Victorian' date are unsupported.
condition: Surface looks dirty and darkened under glass, with small white flecks in the lower area. No obvious holes, flaking or frame damage seen.
reason: Unrecorded name and an amateur-looking sepia copy of a Victorian-style subject, so attribution and age are unsupported.
marks_read: painted 'BALLAT...' (end hidden by frame); other painted lettering illegible
